text: Max Black's two-spheres scenario is standardly taken to refute which theory of individuation, and why?
choices: Substratum theory, because two bare particulars would be qualitatively identical and so collapse into one.
Trope bundle theory, because qualitatively identical tropes would have to be numerically identical.
The bundle theory of universals, because two qualitatively identical bundles of universals would be one and the same bundle, yet the spheres are two.
Aristotelian immanent realism, because a universal cannot be wholly present in two spheres at once.
explanation: Black imagines two indiscernible spheres; a universals-bundle theory identifies each sphere with its bundle of universals, so two identical bundles would be numerically one, contradicting the evident two-ness. The tempting distractor is trope bundle theory (option 1), which in fact escapes the problem precisely because tropes are particulars: the two bundles contain numerically distinct though exactly resembling tropes.
